annotations.title: Send a test event to the webhook

description: Send one test event to the webhook endpoint, to check that your server receives it and verifies its signature. It is signed like a real delivery, so `verifyWebhook` accepts it. The body is `{ id, type: "webhook.test", seq: 0, generation, timestamp, data: { test: true, message } }`: `id` is the delivery's, `seq` is always 0 (a real event's starts at 1) and `message` is a fixed English sentence, the same in every language. It holds no mailbox, contact, message or campaign data. It is tried once and never again: it is not retried, not counted toward switching the endpoint off, and sent again only by calling this again. It is never in `list_events` and an endpoint can't subscribe to it. It goes out even when the endpoint is switched off after delivery failures, and does not switch it on. If the API key that saved it stopped working, nothing reaches its URL, tests included, until a person or a live key saves it again. The answer is the delivery's `deliveryId`: read how it went in `list_webhook_deliveries`, where its `eventType` is `webhook.test`. A workspace sends at most 10 an hour. Answers 404 when no endpoint is set up. A signed-in owner can call this, or an API key with both setup and read permission. A key works only on a webhook a key saved: one a person saved answers 409 `webhookSavedByPerson`, so ask the owner with `create_handoff`, kind `manage_webhook`.

idempotencyKey.description: Your own id for this one call, such as a UUID, up to 255 characters. If the call fails with no answer, call again with the same key and the same arguments: within 24 hours, a saved answer comes back instead of a second run. A call left unanswered can run again after 15 minutes, so a send also keeps its intentKey or draft revision.
